cards.text: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has dreams that trouble his spirit, and sleep escapes him. Friend, you know that night: you flip the pillow to the cold side like THAT'S gonna fix your whole life. So he summons his magicians, enchanters, sorcerers and astrologers to explain his dreams.

cards.question: The king tells his wise men his spirit is anxious to understand his dream. What do the astrologers ask him to do?

cards.text: Here's the problem: the king says his word is final. Friend, when a king says THAT, you just nod.

cards.question: So what does Nebuchadnezzar demand from his wise men?

answers.text: Both the dream and its interpretation
Only the interpretation of his dream
A potion to help him sleep at night

cards.text: If they can't tell him both, they'll be cut into pieces and their houses reduced to rubble. But if they can, he promises gifts, rewards and great honor.
So the wise men try a second time: let the king tell the dream, and they'll give the interpretation. Ah, the classic move: when the answer's no, ask again and hope it turned into a yes.

cards.question: When the wise men ask a second time, the king says he knows for sure they're ___ for time.
True or false: The king says the wise men have been speaking honestly with him.

cards.text: The astrologers say no one on earth can do what the king asks. No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of a magician, enchanter or astrologer.

cards.question: True or false: The astrologers say no one could tell the king his dream except the gods.

cards.text: That answer makes the king so angry and furious that he gives orders to destroy ALL the wise men of Babylon.

cards.question: The decree goes out to execute the wise men. Which young men from Judah, serving the king (Daniel 1:6, 19), do the king's men come looking for too?

cards.text: When Arioch, commander of the king's guard, goes out to execute the wise men of Babylon, Daniel responds with discretion and tact.

cards.question: With the execution order out, what does Daniel ask Arioch?

answers.text: Why the king's decree is so harsh
Who gave the king the idea
When the order will be carried out

cards.text: Arioch explains the situation to Daniel. Then Daniel walks right in to see the very king whose decree has men out looking to execute him.

cards.question: Standing before the king, Daniel asks him for some ___, so he can give him the interpretation.

cards.text: Daniel goes home and explains the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. I bet it opened like every scary phone call ever: 'Are you sitting down?'

cards.question: Daniel urges Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah to plead for ___ from the God of heaven concerning this mystery.

cards.text: During the night, the mystery is revealed to Daniel in a vision. The astrologers said no one on earth could do it, and God hands it over before sunrise.

cards.question: Daniel now knows the king's dream. What does he do?

answers.text: He blesses the God of heaven
He goes right back to sleep
He writes it down on a scroll

cards.text: Daniel declares, 'Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.' Forever AND ever, friend. This is NOT a quick thumbs-up emoji.

cards.question: In Daniel's praise, God changes the times and seasons, and He removes kings and ___ them.
True or false: Daniel says God can't see what lies in darkness.

cards.text: Daniel thanks the God of his fathers, who has made known to them the dream of the king. Then he goes to Arioch, the man the king appointed to destroy the wise men.

cards.question: Daniel tells Arioch, "Do not ___ the wise men of Babylon!"

cards.text: Arioch hastily brings Daniel to the king and says, 'I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.' Arioch, buddy, that man walked up and found YOU.
The king asks Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, if he can tell him what he saw in the dream and its interpretation. Big question, BIG king.

cards.question: Before he tells the dream, what does Daniel say about the wise men, enchanters, mediums and magicians?

answers.text: None of them can explain this mystery
They knew the dream all along
They should be put in charge of it

cards.text: Then Daniel says, 'But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries…'

cards.question: Daniel says God has made something known to King Nebuchadnezzar through his dream. What is it?

answers.text: What will happen in the future
Which of his officials lied to him

cards.question: True or false: Daniel says the mystery was revealed to him because he has more wisdom than any man alive.

cards.text: Then Daniel tells the dream: 'As you, O king, were watching, a great statue appeared.' Dazzling, awesome, and I promise you, friend, it was not a lawn flamingo.
Daniel describes it from the top down: a head of pure gold, chest and arms of silver, belly and thighs of bronze, and legs of iron.

cards.question: At the very bottom of the statue in the king's dream, what are its feet made of?

cards.text: As the king watches, a stone is cut out, but not by human hands. Nobody's holding a chisel on this one, friend.

cards.question: True or false: In the dream, the stone strikes the statue on its feet.

cards.text: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver and gold are all shattered and become like chaff on the threshing floor in summer. The wind carries them away, and not a trace of them can be found.

cards.question: The statue is gone. The stone that struck it becomes a great ___ that fills the whole earth.

cards.text: Daniel says, 'This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.' He starts with the king himself: the God of heaven has given him sovereignty, power, strength and glory, and I bet Nebuchadnezzar LOVED hearing that.

cards.question: Daniel says God made Nebuchadnezzar ruler over people, beasts and birds. Which part of the statue is the king?

cards.text: Daniel says another kingdom will arise after him, inferior to his, and that's the one thing every king loves to hear: the next guy won't measure up. Then a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule the whole earth.

cards.question: Daniel says a fourth kingdom will come, as strong as iron. What will it do to all the others?
True or false: Daniel says the kingdom pictured by the statue's feet will be united and whole.

cards.text: Daniel says this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle, and the peoples will mix with one another but won't hold together, any more than iron mixes with clay. That's dry cookie dough, friend: press it together all you want, it STILL crumbles.

Then Daniel gets to the big one, and friend, if this were a movie, THIS is where the music swells. In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people.

cards.question: This kingdom from the God of heaven will ___ all these kingdoms and bring them to an end.

cards.text: Daniel says that just as the king saw a stone cut out of the mountain without human hands, and it shattered the iron, bronze, clay, silver and gold, so the great God has told the king what will happen in the future. Then he tells him, 'The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.'

cards.question: After hearing the dream and its meaning, how does King Nebuchadnezzar react?

cards.text: He pays homage to Daniel and orders an offering and incense presented to him. Earlier the king's men were out looking to execute Daniel, and now the king is face down in front of him: friend, that's a COMEBACK.

cards.question: True or false: Nebuchadnezzar says Daniel's God is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings.

cards.text: Then the king promotes Daniel and gives him many generous gifts. Talk about a promotion, while MY big career move was from the kitchen counter to the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar makes Daniel ruler over the entire province of ___.
True or false: The king also makes Daniel chief administrator over all the wise men.

cards.text: So now Daniel's the boss of the very wise men he kept from being executed. And he has a request for the king.

cards.question: At Daniel's request, who does the king appoint to manage the province Daniel now rules?

cards.text: The king appoints Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, the new names given to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah (Daniel 1:7), while Daniel stays in the king's court. The friends Daniel called on when things got scary get to stand with him when things get good.
